Hello, i'm trying to make my game fullscreen, not 16:9 ratio, but basic fullscreen you can accomplish in game by pressing f4, normally, that would blur pixels, so i got tdp pixel perfect plugin, wich works perfectly and it removes the blur that would otherwise be applied when pressing f4, the only problem with this is that when moving, every pixel gets "laggy" almost looks like a crt effect, this applies to the whole map but is more evident on sprites that have something that doesent happen if the game is normally windowed, i'm not really sure how to explain it better, i'd guess it has to do with motion blur, also, i've noticed that this doesen't seem to appear in recordings, only when playing and seeing it real time
Thanks in advance to everyone, if you have any suggestions

posts.author: JGreene
posts.body:
Is that Pixel Perfect the Chrome extension? It might not be fully compatible with however MV is processed. There are other ways to increase your game screen's resolution up to your monitor's native resolution.
Yanfly Core Engine
has a parameter that allow you to change the resolution. Just note that, by default, each tile is 48x48. So your dimensions need to be divisible by 48 on each side for it to look the cleanest. For your convenience, the math for a 1600x900 screen would come to 1584x864.

posts.author: JGreene
posts.body:
Think of the screen as the player's field of view. It's always a static width and height (aka window size, or screen resolution). Whatever size game window you feel comfortable with, just measure how many tiles it is in width and height. Then multiply each by 48 to get the resolution for your plugin. It doesn't have to be 16:9. In fact, yours looks closer to 4:3.
Edit: Also, I didn't see the part about community basic. But, you probably won't need it at all if you're using Yanfly's.
